title: Preserve sanitized worker failure evidence on nonzero trusted qualification exits
goal: Repair the trusted TIA V21 Open Library qualification harness so a nonzero worker exit does not collapse an already-created sanitized worker manifest into generic RUN1_EXIT/RUN2_EXIT evidence. Preserve the successful fresh/reuse contract unchanged, stop after a failed first invocation, and publish only bounded validated worker failure tokens. This task is harness-only: it must not change TiaV21Worker migration/reuse semantics, Valve/Stage-B behavior, runner configuration, vendor payloads, or IndustrialMDE.

baselineEvidence.precursorProductMerge: PR #94 merged exact reviewed candidate d4055d72d79e650205a9bc96af65b8bc4cdf0ea2 as main commit 72fb23334984f806ab24a4769c0091b9a9f3a93b.
baselineEvidence.trustedRun: TIA V21 Open Library Qualification #311 / run 36239362693 on main 72fb23334984f806ab24a4769c0091b9a9f3a93b.
trustedRunFacts: Trusted checkout and TiaV21Worker net48 build against installed TIA V21 assemblies succeeded.
Both qualification invocations created manifests and returned exit code 1; neither invocation timed out.
The public evidence step completed and published status FAIL with failure 'Qualification manifest pair failed trusted validation: RUN1_EXIT.'.
The public evidence left TIA build identity, qualification identity, archive identity, reuse flags and provenance as n/a because pair validation checks Run1ExitCode before projecting manifest data.
Raw stdout/stderr and raw manifests remained runner-local and were cleaned; no precise worker failure token is recoverable from public evidence after the run.
baselineEvidence.defect: Test-QualificationPair returns RUN1_EXIT/RUN2_EXIT before the harness safely projects the already-created manifest.failure field. The harness therefore loses a bounded worker-generated failure token that may contain the only supported prerequisite/category evidence needed by Stage A acceptance.

executionPlan.ordering: Merge this protected task authority first. Then implement the harness correction in a separate primary-authored protected workflow PR. Do not rerun trusted TIA qualification until that implementation PR is independently approved, merged, and post-merge CI is green.

stages.title: Project validated worker failure evidence before pair-success validation
stages.author: primary-chatgpt
requirements: Change only the two exact allowed paths. Do not modify TiaV21Worker, any other workflow, agents, tasks, runner configuration, vendor payload handling, Valve/Stage-B code, or IndustrialMDE.
Keep the workflow trusted-main-only. No unmerged candidate code may execute on Windows/TIA.
After run1 creates a manifest, parse and validate its bounded public fields before deciding how to handle a nonzero exit.

If run1 exits nonzero, do not execute run2. Publish a terminal FAIL or BLOCKED evidence object that preserves trustedMainSha/source basename/source SHA and, only when individually validated as safe, TIA build identity, qualification identity and the worker manifest.failure token. Do not claim archive/native-reopen/reuse/provenance success fields.
If run1 exits zero, preserve the existing fresh-or-reuse run1 validation and execute run2 exactly as the current successful path requires.

If run2 exits nonzero, publish a terminal FAIL or BLOCKED result using the same safe worker-failure projection rules while preserving only already-validated run1 identity/provenance fields. Do not report deterministicSecondRun=true.
Never publish manifest.failureDetails, raw stdout/stderr, arbitrary exception messages, absolute paths, usernames, vendor payload content or unvalidated strings.

Accept a worker failure token for public projection only when it matches a strict bounded grammar derived from the current worker's sanitized failure contract: phase token, exception type token, uppercase HRESULT, and optional allowlisted tag/count/16-hex fingerprint suffixes. Reject unknown shape, control characters, path separators, overlong text or any token that cannot be proven safe.
Unsafe/malformed/missing failure tokens must collapse to a fixed generic public code without echoing the unsafe value.

Preserve the current successful pair semantics unchanged: truthful fresh/reuse modes, exact identities/hashes, immutable original provenance, canonical UTC completed timestamp and deterministicSecondRun=true only after the full pair passes.
Keep Job Object timeout/process containment behavior unchanged.

Add deterministic Python regressions that prove: run1 nonzero + safe manifest failure projects the safe token and skips run2; run1 nonzero + unsafe/path-bearing failure is redacted to a fixed generic code; run2 nonzero projects only safe failure after a valid run1; successful fresh->reuse and reuse->reuse paths remain accepted unchanged; failureDetails/raw path/vendor sentinels never enter public evidence.
completionGate: Fresh isolated chatgpt-secondary exact-SHA CODE_REVIEW returns APPROVE with no critical/major findings.
Primary performs delegated merge only after both gates pass.
Only then trigger one new trusted /run-olq-001 on issue #19 and inspect the resulting sanitized evidence before any Valve/Stage-B authority is activated.

requirements: Trusted failure evidence no longer degrades an existing sanitized worker manifest to bare RUN1_EXIT/RUN2_EXIT.
A failed first invocation never starts the second invocation.
Only strictly validated bounded manifest.failure tokens can become public; manifest.failureDetails and arbitrary text never become public evidence.
Unsafe failure text is replaced by a fixed generic public code without echoing the original value.
Successful two-run fresh/reuse and repeated-reuse behavior is unchanged.
tia: After the reviewed harness refinement is merged, rerun trusted qualification exactly once on current main.

If the worker still exits nonzero, the public result must contain a precise bounded supported failure token/category from the trusted worker manifest or a fixed generic unsafe-token code; it must not collapse to RUN1_EXIT alone.
If the first invocation succeeds, the existing two-run fresh/reuse acceptance remains authoritative.
Valve/Stage-B remains blocked unless a trusted run proves a native V21 archive/current-version reopen with the required deterministic reuse provenance.
